name: April Cottage
questions: When was April Cottage built, and when were the rear extension and dormer floor added? Is any of it an original old cottage, or is the stone a facing on a newer build?
The floor plan says 245 m² and the listing says 253 m². Which is right, and how much of the upstairs has full head height under the sloped ceilings?
How close are the neighbours behind the rear block wall and to each side, and who owns the boundary walls? What is planned on the two large housing sites BuyerIQ shows about 200 m away?
How much traffic uses the R130 at the gate, and is there a footpath all the way into Garristown village? Can you hear the boarding kennels or smell the village wastewater plant from the garden?
Has a radon test been done (BuyerIQ flags a moderate radon area), and how old is the oil boiler? Which broadband is connected now?

ai.why: A roomy 253 m² four-double with big common rooms (a 9.6 × 6.1 m kitchen/living, a 6.5 × 6.0 m lounge, a sunroom), three bathrooms and a ground-floor double beside a full bathroom, a short walk from Garristown village and about 40 minutes from central Dublin. Held back by €580k, a modest walled 1/3 acre with neighbours 20–40 m off and on the R130 at the gate, a cottage-style build rather than a genuine old cottage, and about 30 minutes to the nearest all-ages ED. Held at 2.5: big rooms and three baths, but close neighbours behind block walls (~20–30 m), a mostly gravel 1/3 ac on the R130, a cottage-style build rather than an old cottage, and ~30 min to an ED — the Monmore/Alta Villa pattern.

electricity.detail: Mains; overhead lines run along the R130 in front of the house.

water.detail: Mains; 'Mains Water' is in MyHome's features list.

sewer.detail: Mains; 'Mains Waste' is in MyHome's features list.

internet.detail: Likely fibre; not in the listing, and BuyerIQ hides the speed behind its paywall. Check the Eircode on eir's and NBI's maps.

groundFloorBedroom.detail: Bedroom 1 (4.78 × 3.75 m double, at the front) opens off the entrance hall next to a 3.75 × 2.45 m bathroom with a bath and a separate shower; it has no door of its own to the garden.

bedsNote: Four doubles: one on the ground floor beside the main bathroom, and three large dormer bedrooms upstairs (6.70 × 3.62 m with walk-in wardrobe and en-suite, 6.60 × 3.80 m, 6.27 × 3.95 m), plus a 2.50 × 1.90 m office downstairs
heating: Oil-fired central heating (OFCH), plus a multi-fuel stove in the lounge
tagline: A stone-fronted, cottage-style four-bed dormer house of about 250 m² on a walled third of an acre on the R130, a short walk from Garristown village in north Fingal.

pros.detail: Per the floor plan: a 9.63 × 6.08 m kitchen/dining/living room (about 58 m², dual aspect, double doors to the garden), a 6.45 × 5.96 m lounge (about 38 m²) with a multi-fuel stove, and a 3.85 × 3.32 m sunroom off it.

pros.text: A ground-floor double beside a full bathroom
pros.detail: Bedroom 1 is 4.78 × 3.75 m (about 18 m²), off the hall next to a 3.75 × 2.45 m bathroom with a large bath and a separate shower.

The ground-floor bathroom, an en-suite (2.25 × 2.18 m) with a walk-in wardrobe off the 6.70 × 3.62 m master, and a 2.11 × 2.07 m shower room on the landing; the three upstairs bedrooms are each over 23 m².
Garristown National School 760 m and the Route 195 bus 510 m per the listing; the Mace and post office are on the same Naul Road, and Quinn's bar is in the village.

pros.text: Mains water and sewer, oil heating
pros.detail: MyHome's features list says mains water, mains waste and OFCH; BER C1 at 161.88 kWh/m²/yr.
A natural stone facade with brick reveals behind a stone wall with wrought-iron railings, gated gravel parking, and a south-facing walled rear garden with a raised lawn and shed.

pros.text: Close to Dublin and the airport
pros.detail: Ashbourne about 12 km, Dublin Airport about 25 km and St Stephen's Green about 40 km; Gormanston station about 15 km for Northern Commuter trains.

cons.detail: The listing photos show a bungalow just behind the rear block wall (about 20–25 m from the house) and a dormer house across the R130 about 30 m away; the aerial shows houses on each side within about 20–40 m, with block walls rather than hedges or trees at the back.
About €2,290/m² plus stamp duty of €5,800; within the ~€650k allowed near Dublin for something special, but well above the €500k norm.

cons.text: A modest walled plot on the R130
cons.detail: About 1/3 acre (0.13 ha) by the listing, much of it gravel; the rear lawn is a raised strip, and the front wall stands on the R130 Naul Road, a regional road with a centre line.

cons.text: About 30 minutes to an all-ages ED
cons.detail: Our Lady of Lourdes, Drogheda is about 27 km; Temple Street (children) and Beaumont/Connolly (adults) are about 35 km; Ashbourne has GPs and pharmacies about 12 km away.

The cut-stone facing, uPVC sash-style windows, dormer roof lights and rendered rear with pink trim suggest a 1990s–2000s build or a heavily rebuilt one; the build year isn't stated. Laminate floors in most rooms.

BuyerIQ lists 10 planning applications within 1 km, including 2 large residential schemes about 200 m away (a building site is visible in the aerial); a boarding kennels and the village wastewater plant are marked nearby on the brochure map.
The plan says 245 m² and the listing 253 m², and the upstairs rooms have sloping ceilings; BuyerIQ flags a moderate radon area.
